candidates.title: Route hard QA through a human-model chat loop rather than direct model prompting
candidates.rule: For hard multiple-choice QA where neither a non-expert human nor a zero-shot prompt is reliable, have the human interrogate the assistant through multi-turn chat with conversation resets instead of accepting a single prompted answer; expect roughly 10-point gains over the best prompting baseline, but do not treat the resulting answers as trustworthy for high-stakes use.
candidates.passage: model-assisted humans outperform our best model results by similarly large margins (75% vs. 66% on MMLU, 77% vs. 67% on QuALITY)
candidates.finding: Across 100 validation questions each from MMLU and time-limited QuALITY, four non-expert participants per task using a chat interface scored 75.4% and 76.8%, versus best model-only baselines of 65.6% and 66.9% and unassisted humans of 57.2% and 48.6%. Calibration error rose for human-model teams on MMLU, and participants sometimes confidently accepted false model claims.
models: 52B-parameter Anthropic RLHF 'helpful-only' dialog assistant (Bai et al., 2022)
workloads: QuALITY reading comprehension under a 5-minute time limit (100 validation questions)
candidates.conditions: Chat UI with reset button; for QuALITY the passage was injected as the first turn; correct answers were revealed after each question; participants paid at least $20/hr; two of ten participants who far outperformed the model were excluded.
candidates.limitations: Single paper, small sample (100 items, 4 annotators per task), one model, multiple-choice only; answer-reveal and outlier removal bias results; no matched time/cost budget against prompting baselines; teams remained below reported expert levels (90% MMLU, 93.5% untimed QuALITY) and were worse calibrated on MMLU.
candidates.validation_test: On a fresh set of hard QA items with a current assistant, compare zero-shot, chain-of-thought prompting, and human-in-chat conditions at matched wall-clock/cost per item, without revealing gold answers, and report both accuracy and calibration error.

reason: The paper reports a human-model interaction experiment with concrete comparisons (unassisted human, model-only prompting variants, human+model, and aggregation), plus documented participant strategies. Two scoped rules are supportable as author-tested at the measured level; the participant-strategy rule is inferred since individual strategies were not separately compared.
